message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, but you can quickly check the current air quality in Los Angeles using a few reliable sources:

| Source | How to Use | Typical Information Provided |
|--------|------------|------------------------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Go to [airnow.gov](https://www.airnow.gov/), enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. | Current AQI value, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO), health advisories, forecast. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Visit [aqicn.org/city/los-angeles](https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/). | Real‑time AQI, historical trends, maps, and alerts. |
| **Local news & weather apps** | Check the LA Times, CBS Los Angeles, or weather apps like Weather.com. | Often include a quick “Air Quality” widget with AQI and health tips. |
| **California Air Resources Board (CARB)** | Visit [carb.ca.gov](https://www.carb.ca.gov/) and look for the “Air Quality” section. | State‑wide monitoring, long‑term trends, and policy updates. |

### Quick Tips for Interpreting AQI

| AQI Range | Health Impact | Recommended Action |
|-----------|---------------|--------------------|
| 0–50 (Good) | No adverse health effects | Normal outdoor activities |
| 51–100 (Moderate) | Unhealthy for sensitive groups (e.g., children, elderly) | Reduce prolonged outdoor exertion |
| 101–150 (Unhealthy) | Everyone may experience health effects | Limit outdoor activity, especially strenuous |
| 151–200 (Very Unhealthy) | Serious health effects | Avoid outdoor activity, consider indoor exercise |
| 201+ (Hazardous) | Extremely serious health effects | Stay indoors, avoid outdoor activity |

If you’re planning to be outside, it’s a good idea to check the forecast for the next 24–48 hours as well—sometimes the AQI can improve or worsen quickly due to weather changes or traffic patterns.

Let me know if you’d like help interpreting a specific AQI reading or if you want to set up alerts for when the air quality drops below a certain threshold!
